name: **[Storra (Cloud Storage Platform)](https://github.com/Raqibreyaz/Personal-Google-Drive)** | Node.js, React.js, Express.js, MongoDB, Redis, AWS S3, AWS EC2
summary: A secure cloud storage platform with role-based access control, file sharing, and robust authentication integration.
highlights: Architected a secure cloud storage API supporting file uploads, downloads, streaming previews, and metadata management.
Engineered a robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system with granular global and user-specific file sharing permissions with 3 roles Owner, Admin and User.
Implemented inclusive authentication flows combining OTP verification with external OAuth integrations (Google, GitHub).
Reduced potential security vulnerabilities by implementing robust defenses against SQL Injection, XSS, CSRF, and DoS attacks.

name: **[ShipIt (Self-Hosted CI/CD Server)](https://github.com/Raqibreyaz/Storra)** | Node.js, PM2, Telegram API, Octokit, AWS S3 + CloudFront
summary: A lightweight, self-hosted CI/CD server that deploys on GitHub push events via webhooks and SSH, featuring smart dependency detection, automatic rollback on unhealthy releases, Telegram notifications, and frontend delivery to S3 + CloudFront.
highlights: Built a webhook-triggered deployment system that SSHs into remote servers, pulls latest code, and skipping `dependency installation` when no dependencies changed.
Engineered a symlink-based release system with automatic rollback on health-check failure, maintaining last working code in versioned release directories.
Integrated Telegram Bot API to send structured deployment summaries with log tails on success/failure, and set GitHub commit statuses using Octokit for pending/success/failure states.
Implemented branch-based deployments, S3 + CloudFront frontend hosting with AWS CLI, and Redis-stored deployment logs with 7-day TTL for step-by-step inspection.

name: **[Banaras Mart (Ecommerce App)](https://github.com/Raqibreyaz/Banaras-Mart)** | Node.js, React.js, Express, MongoDB, Razorpay
summary: A role-based multi-vendor e-commerce platform with secure JWT authentication, product management, and Razorpay payment integration.
highlights: Developed a comprehensive e-commerce backend supporting product management, cart states, and user wishlists.
Engineered efficient product discovery APIs featuring advanced database filtering and dynamic pagination.
Integrated the Razorpay API to securely process transactions and orchestrate seamless checkout workflows.
Implemented a secure user management system handling registration, authentication, and password recovery.

name: **[ProxyRaQ(Multithreaded Proxy Web Server)](https://github.com/Raqibreyaz/ProxyRaQ)** | C, Thread Pool, Concurrency, LRU Caching, Sockets, HTTP
summary: A multi-threaded HTTP proxy server that handles concurrent clients with custom sockets and improves performance using LRU-based caching and low-level request/response handling.
highlights: a multi-threaded HTTP proxy server in C with a thread pool and client queue to handle concurrent connections efficiently and reduce request starvation.
Implemented an LRU-based cache with mutex-protected shared access and cache invalidation using last-modified time checks to avoid serving stale content.
Developed low-level socket communication and HTTP request/response parsing, including dynamic buffer growth for large or transfer-encoded server responses.
Improved reliability by handling client disconnects with SIGPIPE ignoring, adding graceful SIGINT shutdown behavior, and returning custom error responses to clients.
Added production-focused utilities such as URL normalization, blocked-site filtering from JSON, filename sanitization for cache storage, and environment-based port configuration.

name: **[Synclet](https://github.com/Raqibreyaz/Synclet)** | C++, Linux inotify API, epoll, Content-Defined Chunking, SHA-256, TCP / Custom Binary Protocol
summary: A content-defined, chunk-based file synchronization and backup tool that detects real file deltas and syncs them efficiently using event-driven file watching, snapshots, and a custom peer protocol.
highlights: Built a content-defined chunked file sync engine in C++ using Rabin-Karp rolling hash for chunk boundary detection and SHA-256 for chunk integrity, syncing only delta changes to minimize bandwidth and sync time
Integrated Linux's inotify API with epoll for non-blocking, event-driven file watching across recursive directory trees, eliminating CPU-wasteful polling and batching noisy filesystem events

Designed a custom binary wire protocol with typed messages (MODIFIED_CHUNK, FILE_RENAME, REQ_SNAP, etc.) and length-prefixed framing to reliably stream chunk metadata and raw binary data between peers over TCP

Implemented snapshot versioning by hashing filename, size, mtime, and chunk hashes via SHA-256 to detect cross-session state drift, enabling efficient initial sync without re-fetching full peer snapshots on every startup

Engineered initial bidirectional sync logic with mtime-based conflict resolution, ordered_set chunk reassembly from disk-persisted .bin files, and a cookie-based hashmap for pairing inotify MOVED_FROM/MOVED_TO events within a 200ms window
